items.titleEn: Palantir delivers blowout quarter - but there's a catch
items.summaryEn: Buy Palantir (PLTR). The quarter shows corporate AI spending is translating into real revenue, and commercial revenue is now the biggest slice. The key is that management’s Q4 outlook still implies strong sequential growth, so the market’s “replenishment” worry can be answered if bookings catch up over the next few quarters. You’re buying the probability-weighted path where commercial deployments deepen and revenue keeps compounding. Key Risk: New US commercial contract signings stay weak for multiple quarters, so revenue growth is just converting older deals and the valuation can’t be supported. Sell Palantir (PLTR) if the next earnings cycle confirms the gap: US commercial revenue up sharply while new US commercial contract value remains near-flat. That pattern means customers are buying work already in motion, not expanding commitments. If guidance holds but bookings don’t, the stock rerates lower because the market stops believing in sustained growth.

items.titleEn: SpaceX stock rises as Musk explores Boost Mobile deal for wireless push
items.summaryEn: Buy SpaceX (SPCX). The Boost Mobile/EchoStar path is a credible shortcut to a US wireless launch (MVNO or carrier buildout) that can turn Starlink’s huge user base into a mobile distribution engine. Upside is asymmetric because even partial access (spectrum/network deals) can accelerate “Starlink Mobile” and force incumbents to defend ARPU and churn. Key Risk: AT&T/T-Mobile block or delay transferring Boost’s network-leasing agreements, making SpaceX’s wireless timeline slip by years. Buy Crown Castle (CCI) and/or American Tower (AMT). If SpaceX pursues tower access or leases, it becomes a new high-quality tenant. The market already priced some of this (CCI down on the day despite prior run), so any confirmation of negotiations should re-rate tower demand expectations.

items.titleEn: Marvell, Lumentum merge in $115 billion deal amid AI spending jitters
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: U.S. chipmaker Marvell Technology said Monday it will buy optical components maker Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal, the latest bid for scale among AI infrastructure companies as investors increasingly question whether the industry's spending boom will pay off. The deal, among the largest technology mergers on record, comes days after a selloff that hammered shares of companies tied to artificial intelligence.

items.titleEn: Anthropic says revenue surged 1,100% ahead of IPO
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100% surge in quarterly revenue and nearly $900 billion in spending commitments as it counts down to its Wall Street listing later this month. The San Francisco-based company was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers led by chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela, now its president, with AI safety as its focus.

items.titleEn: Snap settles US social media trial days after Meta
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Snap has settled what would have been another landmark trial over the alleged harms of social media, lawyers for the plaintiffs said Monday, just days after Meta reached its own settlement and two days before opening statements were due to begin in a Los Angeles courtroom. The case was to be the latest in a series of bellwether, or test, trials whose outcomes are expected to guide the resolution of hundreds of similar lawsuits across the United States.

items.titleEn: Meta delays new business terms after outcry over potential web scraping of news sites
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Meta said it was postponing the rollout of new terms for its business accounts after an outcry from media companies and open-web advocates who said the updated rules would allow the tech giant to scrape vast amounts of data and potentially build competing services. The new rules, originally scheduled to go into effect Oct. 30, authorize Meta to use automated software such as web scrapers and bots to "index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl the domains, web pages, or URLs" associated with a business account.

Buy Rivian Automotive (RIVN). UBS/Jefferies upgrades hinge on R2 ramp driving higher automotive gross margins and volume growth, with most 2028 units expected from R2. The stock just re-rated on improving demand signals; you want in before the market fully prices the margin inflection and the software/services upside (Autonomy+). Key Risk: R2 demand or production ramp disappoints, so margins don’t improve and Rivian burns cash longer than expected. Buy Rivian Automotive (RIVN) again, but specifically for the second catalyst: Autonomy+ as a Tesla Full Self-Driving competitor. The December Autonomy Day and early-2027 launch create a clear event path where any credible progress can re-rate the stock toward higher-margin software economics.

items.titleEn: Why is Amazon stock surging 4% today?
items.summaryEn: Amazon stock AMZN rose more than 4% on Monday after Phillip Securities upgraded the shares, citing strong demand visibility in cloud computing and the company's positioning across the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. The stock gained 4.5% in morning trading after Phillip Securities raised its rating to Buy from Accumulate and increased its price target to $330 from $320. Analyst Helena Wang said Amazon's positioning across the AI infrastructure market and strong growth at Amazon Web Services (AWS) supported a more positive outlook, despite concerns about near-term cash flow.
